activity.role: English navigator and Tokugawa diplomatic adviser
activity.notes: Representative 1613 point corresponds to the English trading post established in Hirado during diplomatic-adviser William Adams's documented service under the Tokugawa regime; it is NOT his arrival in Japan (1600), the beginning of his entire advisory term, or a 1613-only lifetime. Japanese name Miura Anjin refers to the SAME individual; never register as a separate Person. The Tokugawa Shogunate began in 1603, so use this existing contemporary polity for a 1613 Activity.

sources.title: Embassy of Japan in the UK — Japan400 seminar, 12 December 2023
sources.citation_text: Japanese Embassy confirms William Adams/Miura Anjin arrived 1600, served Tokugawa Ieyasu as diplomatic adviser, and the English trading post at Hirado was opened in 1613.

sources.title: William Adams Memorial, Ito City
sources.citation_text: Ito City memorial commemorates the navigator's 1600 arrival, his Tokugawa diplomatic service and subsequent early-17th-century shipbuilding and trade.

spatial_disposition.evidence: Independent 1613 Hirado English trading post and Tokugawa diplomacy are historically attested, but an exact personal PlaceFunction or specific authoritative UUID/coordinate was not reviewed; location mapping held, no invented point.
